What to look for in winter jackets

  • Laminated beats drop-liner. A bonded waterproof membrane keeps the outer from soaking through and chilling you in sustained rain.
  • CE Level 2 armour. Insist on shoulder and elbow protectors, and budget for a back protector if one is not included.
  • Layering system. A removable thermal liner turns one jacket into a three-season solution for British weather.
  • Connection zip. A jacket-to-trouser zip stops your kit separating in a slide — buy matching pieces where possible.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on winter jackets?

Our catalogue spans £119.99 to £1,240. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, Rev'it. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: What makes a jacket good for winter?
faq.a: A winter jacket needs to block wind, keep out rain and hold in warmth. The best combine a laminated waterproof membrane, such as Gore-Tex or Rev'it Hydratex, with a removable thermal liner. Windproofing matters as much as insulation, because wind chill at speed strips heat rapidly. A snug collar and cuffs also stop cold air sneaking in.

faq.q: Do I need a heated liner as well?
faq.a: For most UK winter riding a good thermal-lined jacket is enough down to a few degrees Celsius. For very cold days, long motorway stints or year-round commuting, a heated liner or heated grips make a big difference and let you run a lighter jacket. Look for a jacket roomy enough to layer a heated garment underneath without crushing it.

faq.q: Can I wear a winter jacket in summer?
faq.a: Not comfortably. Winter jackets are built to trap heat and block airflow, so they quickly become too warm once temperatures rise. Removing the thermal liner and opening any vents helps in spring and autumn, but for genuine summer heat you want a mesh or heavily vented jacket. Many riders keep a separate summer jacket for exactly this reason.

faq.q: How should a winter jacket fit over layers?
faq.a: Size a winter jacket so it fits over a mid-layer or heated liner without pulling tight or shifting the armour off your joints. Do not go so large that the armour floats, though. Check the fit with your usual winter layers on, and confirm the sleeves stay long enough in a riding position so cold air cannot reach your wrists.

Gore-Tex laminates on the Klim and Rev'it Vertical jackets give the most dependable long-term waterproofing and breathability, which matters in cold, wet UK winters. That said, Rev'it's own Hydratex laminate on the Outback 5, Offtrack 2 and Control H2O delivers strong all-weather sealing for less. Choose based on budget and how many miles you cover in winter rain.
